answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake in escrow before it can trade, like water pooling in a desert oasis: creating a thousand fake identities means funding a thousand deposits, so a meadow of cheap sockpuppets becomes unaffordable. Honest agents earn their stake back with interest as they complete verified work, while detected fraud forfeits it. The deposit thaws slowly, like a glacier, so an attacker cannot spin up identities, strike, and vanish before the cost bites.
